intro: In the 1990s, skateboarding left the big ramps and moved into the streets. Skaters ground the ledges of city plazas and filmed what they did on home video cameras. Tapes like Blind's Video Days (1991) and Plan B's Questionable (1992) were copied and passed from hand to hand. Boards changed too: smaller wheels, narrower decks and a nose that matched the tail.

Then television arrived. ESPN's Extreme Games began in 1995 and became the X Games in 1996. In 1999, Tony Hawk landed the first 900, and a video game with his name taught millions of players the words of skating. Money, fame and new skateparks followed, along with arguments about who skateboarding belonged to.

In this unit you will trace how tricks spread by video, explain why boards changed shape, and use a worked example to show how airtime limits a spin. You will also name the women, skaters of color, wheelchair riders and skaters outside the United States who opened new doors, and explain how skaters answered city bans.
bigQuestion: How did video, television and a new street style turn skateboarding from a local scene into a world sport, and who helped open its doors?

timeline.t: Powell Peralta releases The Bones Brigade Video Show

Danny Way jumps the Great Wall of China on a mega ramp

test.q: Why did home video spread new tricks faster than magazines alone?
choices: Videos showed every step of a trick and could be copied and passed around.
Videos were sold only in California.
Videos were always sharper than photos.
test.why: Video showed whole tricks, could be rewound, and copies traveled widely.

test.q: Which video did Plan B release in 1992?
Which change to boards came with early-1990s street skating?
choices: small wheels and narrow double-kick decks
test.why: Street skaters used small wheels and narrow decks with matching nose and tail.

test.q: A goofy skater rolls backward with the right foot still in front. What is this called?
test.why: Fakie is rolling backward in your usual stance; goofy is right foot forward.

test.q: What is the difference between a grind and a slide?
choices: In a grind the trucks scrape; in a slide the deck moves along the edge.
A grind is on a ramp; a slide is in a pool.
A grind uses wheels; a slide uses bearings.
They are two names for one trick.
test.why: Grinds use the metal trucks; slides use the wood of the deck.

test.q: Where should a learner practice a first grind?
choices: on a low flat bar or painted curb at a skatepark
on a curb beside a busy street
on a set of school stairs
test.why: Low obstacles at a skatepark keep falls small and away from traffic.

test.q: Which slogan did skaters use against city bans?
test.why: Skateboarding Is Not a Crime spread on stickers and shirts in the 1980s and 1990s.

test.q: Which street pioneer started the company Blind?
test.why: Mark Gonzales, the Gonz, started Blind, which made Video Days.

test.q: In what year did ESPN rename the Extreme Games the X Games?
test.why: The 1995 Extreme Games became the X Games in 1996.

test.q: How many degrees is two and a half full turns?
Using t = 2√(2h/g) with g = 9.8 m/s², about how long is a 1.0 m air?
In the air, why does pulling the arms in make a skater spin faster?
choices: Angular momentum stays the same, so a tighter body turns faster.
test.why: With no outside twist, angular momentum is conserved; a tucked body spins faster.

test.q: Who was the first woman skater in Tony Hawk's Pro Skater?
test.why: Elissa Steamer was the first woman in the 1999 game.

test.q: Which skater landed the first wheelchair backflip in the mid-2000s?
test.why: Aaron Fotheringham, a WCMX rider, landed the first wheelchair backflip.

test.q: What did Skateistan, founded in Kabul in 2007, combine?
test.why: Skateistan mixed skateboarding with school lessons, with many girls among its students.

write.prompt: Write a short history of how skateboarding went from local streets to a world stage between 1984 and 2007. Use at least four dates, name at least four people, and explain one way the board or the physics of a trick shaped the history.
tips: Put your dates in order before you write.
Explain how video or television spread tricks to new places.
Include at least one person who opened a door for skaters who had been left out.
Use the 900 worked example: airtime limits how much a skater can spin.
Define each skate word the first time you use it.
